# Trade-offs and Unintended Consequences

## By the end of today

You will be able to recognize trade-offs and unintended consequences in public policy and begin to understand why they matter.

We limit government because it is organized coercive force and because even good people are not omniscient.

"If men were angels, no government would be necessary." Good intentions and incorruptibility are not enough. Knowledge is local. Policy moves one thing and moves others you did not price.

Ideology and interest both hide trade-offs. Look for concentrated benefits, diffuse costs, and the next move by the people being regulated.
